observationsNotFindings: The containment discipline is what makes this artifact acceptable, and it is worth the coordinator seeing how tightly it is drawn. Every number and consequence that would follow from naming a twenty-seventh gate lives inside threeLimbActIfRecorded, proposedFile08RowIfRecorded, condition4EffectIfRecorded or eligibilityEffect, each of which is conditional in its own name, and the sentence 'This file existing is not the recording' appears five times across purpose, the top-level flag, the remeasurement clause, the eligibility effect and the condition-4 effect. Nothing about 27 of 27 or 31 of 31 is stated as live.

The one carried sentence worth a successor's attention is proposedLaterWork's 'A later harness-spec authoring cycle may occupy artifactPathWhenAuthored. This file does not.' It was straightforwardly forward-looking in v1, where artifactExists was false; in v2 the path is occupied and the sentence is stale in emphasis though not false. I record the reasoning for not charging it in the attack list rather than burying it here.

Naming the excluded twelfth candidate is better practice than silence. notATwelfthClass identifies the namespace-migration doctor-remediation fixture and routes it to DR-114, so the boundary is checkable rather than merely asserted, and gate.executesIfRecorded separately holds that D-130's also-bytes stay also-bytes.

This is a naming candidate for a gate that does not exist on the register, and its specification sibling is itself CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and awaiting review. Two independent acts therefore stand between this file and G31 being live: a D-000 recording of the three-limb act, and an accepted specification at the named path. The artifact says so; the coordinator should hold both in view when sequencing.

OBL-NT-11-EXECUTION remains leftover-design, the eleven classes remain unexecuted, and the G31 specification remains a separate candidate awaiting its own review.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The central risk in a naming candidate is that a proposed twenty-seventh gate leaks into an assertion about live state, and it does not: DR-G31 occurs zero times in live file 08, every 27 and 31 sits inside a container whose own name marks it conditional, and 'This file existing is not the recording' appears five times across five different fields. Live required-now stays 26 and file 08 is unedited. The two occupancy attacks both resolve in the artifact's favour and were the point of this version: artifactPathWhenAuthored is the v2 specification path, artifactExists is true, and that specification genuinely exists at the pinned digest carrying the passProperty, failsIf, matrix and retainedEvidence whose absence caused the v1 REJECT - so CLAUDE-G31-V1-SF1 is properly landed, and live v1 still carries the old path with artifactExists false, confirming a supersession rather than an edit. The eleven classes equal the D-130 corpus at two independent places inside it, rosterSource.classesVerbatim and authoredCatalog.members, with classCount and primaryCount both 11, and the excluded twelfth candidate is named and routed to DR-114 rather than left implicit. One carried sentence is worth a successor's attention and I explain in the attack list why I did not charge it: proposedLaterWork still says a later cycle may occupy the path, which was forward-looking in v1 where artifactExists was false and is now stale in emphasis, but it asserts nothing false and contradicts nothing the file claims. Disclosure: one pin, the gate-harness-naming.v8 verdict, is my own from earlier in this session, and I re-verified its load-bearing content against live file 08 directly. 20 attacks run, 19 refuted, 1 examined and recorded as an observation rather than a finding.
